# muxt's template engine stands in for html/template only in the coverage
# pre-pass, and it is not html/template in every respect: its
# Template.Tree is not a *parse.Tree. A test that reads the parse tree
# does not build under the engine.
#
# That costs the coverage, not the run. One warning line names the
# failure and the known gaps, coverage is unknown so no mutant is
# reported unreached, and the kill runs go on with the real
# html/template, where the test builds and passes.

muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt
stderr '(?m)^warning: template coverage unknown: tests fail under muxt''s template engine \(coverage pre-pass\): \./render_test\.go:20:25: cannot use templates\.Lookup\("greeting"\)\.Tree \(variable of type \*engine\.Tree\) as \*parse\.Tree value in variable declaration; known gaps: Template\.Tree, AddParseTree, Error\.Node$'
! stdout unreached

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Greeting struct {
	Name string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, greeting Greeting) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", greeting)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"text/template/parse"
)

func TestGreeting(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Greeting{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestGreetingTree(t *testing.T) {
	var tree *parse.Tree = templates.Lookup("greeting").Tree
	if got := len(tree.Root.Nodes); got == 0 {
		t.Errorf("greeting has %d nodes", got)
	}
}
-- want.txt --
1 mutant across 1 template (complexity 1, seed 1)
baseline ok

1 mutant, 1 killed, 0 missed, 0 skipped
